title: Connect Your AI Apps
subtitle: Run your pipelines, check run status, and approve steps directly from the desktop AI app you already use. One secure sign-in, zero context switching.

endpoint.label: Your MCP server URL
endpoint.hint: Same URL for every app — each one discovers sign-in automatically (OAuth 2.1).

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.step1Desc: Paste your MCP server URL into your AI app using the guide below.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Your app opens a browser window. Log in and approve access — no API keys to manage.
howItWorks.step3Desc: List pipelines, start runs, and approve steps without leaving your AI app.

claude.name: Claude Desktop
claude.step1: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
claude.step2: Name it “AI Swarm Studio” and paste your MCP server URL.
claude.step3: Click Connect — a browser window opens for sign-in.
claude.step4: Approve access. Tools are now available in every conversation: list_pipelines, run_pipeline, get_pipeline, create_pipeline, update_pipeline, design_pipeline, and more.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.step1: Go to Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and enable Developer Mode.
chatgpt.step2: Create a new app and add your MCP server URL as the connector endpoint.
chatgpt.step3: ChatGPT discovers the OAuth flow automatically — sign in when prompted.
chatgpt.step4: Mention the app in any chat to list and run your pipelines.

qwen.name: Qwen Code
qwen.step1: Add the server from your terminal:
qwen.step2: Qwen Code stores the server in ~/.qwen/settings.json.
qwen.step3: On first use a browser opens for OAuth sign-in — approve access.
qwen.step4: Ask Qwen Code to run a pipeline; it calls the tools directly.

kimi.name: Kimi
kimi.step1: Open Settings → MCP Servers → Add Server.
kimi.step2: Choose the streamable HTTP transport and paste your MCP server URL.
kimi.step3: Save, then click Authorize to complete OAuth sign-in.
kimi.step4: Your pipelines appear as tools in new conversations.

securityNote.title: Your data stays yours
securityNote.desc: Apps only get the permissions you approve (read, run, or write). Access tokens expire after one hour and you can revoke any connected app from Settings at any time.
